lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Keisha, this is Camila. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Camila. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walking went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Pretty good actually.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to walk 20 minutes on 3 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I didn't do it. I just didn't feel like it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My back was hurting so I didn't push it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The pain held you back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My granddaughter is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've got a plan in mind already.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Three 10-minute walks count the same as one 30-minute walk.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I put a reminder on the fridge. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That took effort.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Three 10-minute walks count the same as one 30-minute walk.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, between appointments and everything, there was no time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you use the step counter?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walking going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I walk 10 minutes on 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 0 out of 3 days, the hard part was getting started, and next week you're going to walk 10 minutes on 3 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Keisha. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

flags.reason: Repeats the 10-minute vs 30-minute point without permission after participant showed reluctance; repeated at line 39.
Same information repeated a second time; pushes the coach's preferred framing instead of eliciting participant's view.
Praises 'real progress' although participant reported 0 of 3 walks; affirmation not tied to actual effort.
Asks what was noticed on 'days it went well' when participant reported no walks; presumes success that did not occur.

score.summary: The coach reviewed the missed walking goal, offered autonomy, and helped set a realistic 10-minute, 3-day goal with a barrier plan and follow-up. However, the coach repeated the same information twice (lines 31 and 39) and affirmed 'real progress' despite zero walks, which undercut partnership and empathy.
strengths: Line 8 reviewed the last goal directly and openly.
Line 35 used a strong complex reflection capturing ambivalence and the wish to fit walking into real life.
Line 54 planned for barriers and Line 56 summarized the goal clearly, with the participant confirming it.
coaching_tips: Lines 31 and 39 repeat the same walking-length point; after one offer, ask permission or ask what Keisha thinks instead of repeating it.
Line 26 praised 'real progress' after 0 of 3 walks; reflect the effort she named (line 27, 'At least I'm trying') rather than overstating progress.
Line 24 assumed there were good days; ask an open question that fits her report, such as 'What got in the way on those days?'
Line 13 'Got it' followed the back pain at line 14 without exploring it; a brief open question about the back pain would have helped partnership.
